title: Environment inventory & air-gap blockers
body:
Context: notes from 2025-09-11 pre-workshop with RetailCo infra + security. Goal: capture environment inventory, enumerate blockers for a fully air-gapped (no egress) deployment of Redwood Private, and propose minimally invasive mitigations for a short POC (2-4 weeks).

Quick summary:
- Customer wants fully on-prem inference for PII workloads; strict egress policy (no outbound internet except strictly approved update window).
- Primary blocker categories: model/assets transfer, KMS/HSM integration, image/OS patching, metrics/observability, licensing & entitlements, and operator access for updates.
- POC scope agreed: deploy a single-model endpoint (up to 13B), 2-node inference pool (NVIDIA A40 equivalent), baseline latency target 120ms p95 for 256-token responses, validation with 1k concurrent daily requests.

Inventory template (fields to collect ASAP):
- Physical site(s): datacenter name, rack locations, network zone (production/test).
- Hardware: GPU model(s), driver versions, CUDA/cuDNN versions, NICs (10/25/40/100Gb), CPU, RAM, local disk (NVMe size + throughput), NFS/StorAge details.
- Hypervisor/container runtime: bare-metal / VMware / KVM / OpenShift, container runtime (docker/containerd), OS + kernel version.
- Network topology: VLANs, firewall vendor & rules, private IP ranges, crossover ports allowed, NAT boxes, egress proxies, allowed destination CIDRs (if any).
- Internet policy: fully air-gapped? maintenance windows with temporary egress? whitelisted domains? egress via jumpbox only?
- Registry & artifacts: local container registry (Harbor/ECR proxy), allowed registry authentication (AD/LDAP, local cert), artifact import process (sneakernet / signed bundles).
- Secrets/KMS: do they have an on-prem KMS or HSM (Thales, AWS CloudHSM via DMZ, HashiCorp Vault)? requirement for FIPS/TLS mutual auth?
- PKI/certs: internal CA details, cert rotation process, cert formats accepted.
- Compliance constraints: specific controls (SOC2, FedRAMP, HIPAA) and any required encryption-at-rest standards or audit logging retention.
- Site staffing & operator access: who can run upgrades, windows for on-site tech, ssh bastion policies, privileged access process.
- Monitoring & logs: allowed telemetry to leave site? Local ELK/Datadog on-prem collector? retention requirements.

Blockers and suggested mitigations (ranked):
1) Artifact transfer (models, container images, runtime bits) - Blocker severity: high
   - Problem: no outbound allowed so we cannot pull images or model files live.
   - Mitigations: support signed offline bundle (tar.gz) with checksum and signature. Customer can import via secure usb or internal SCP to registry. Provide a reproducible 'bundle build' script and verification steps. Recommend content of bundle: runtime container images, model weights (quantized and original), start scripts, recommended config file, and a one-click local registry load script.
   - POC ask: customer to provide a local registry endpoint and a process owner for bundle ingestion.

2) Secrets & KMS integration - Blocker severity: high
   - Problem: Redwood expects a KMS for control-plane secrets; customer uses HSM with PKCS#11 and requires no plaintext keys on disk.
   - Mitigations: support KMS adapter pattern in our operator (documented PKCS#11 shim). For POC, run a Vault instance in dev mode with sealed/unseal steps performed by customer or use a customer-provided HSM and test key wrap/unwarp flows. Provide a minimal adapter example.

3) Upgrades / patching policy - Blocker severity: medium
   - Problem: site cannot accept frequent updates; all patches must go through change control.
   - Mitigations: produce a 'point-in-time' POC image locked to specific versions. Define an explicit upgrade cadence and offline upgrade bundle. Include a rollback plan and binary-level signatures to meet CAB requirements.

4) Observability & telemetry egress - Blocker severity: medium
   - Problem: telemetry/metrics cannot be sent to hosted console.
   - Mitigations: provide local metrics endpoint (Prometheus) and optional push-based agent that writes to local ELK. For the POC, we will run the console in a limited local-only mode, and send redacted logs via secure transport only if customer authorizes. Provide instructions for local trace sampling and retention policies.

5) Licensing & entitlements - Blocker severity: low
   - Problem: license activation typically calls home.
   - Mitigations: offer offline license file generation (signed token) that can be applied locally. Support short-lived activation window if customer permits stamped activation via staging host.

Acceptance criteria for POC:
- Successful ingestion of offline bundle by customer registry and ability to start inference containers without external internet.
- KMS/HSM integration validated: operator can retrieve service identity and decrypt a test secret using customer HSM or local Vault.
- Latency and throughput targets met on provided hardware (p95 <= 120ms, 1k total daily requests with baseline concurrency).
- Local observability enabled; basic dashboards available to customer SREs.
- Security review sign-off on no-cleartext secret flows and audit logs captured.

Minimum test plan (high-level):
- Day 0: environment validation (hardware, drivers, network routes), import offline bundle.
- Day 1: bring up control-plane components, register node(s) with operator, validate container health.
- Day 2: load model, run synthetic traffic ramp to target qps, capture perf metrics.
- Day 3: KMS rotation test (simulate key rollover), cert rotation test, simulated pod/node restart.
- Day 4: final security checklist, sign-off runbook and handover to customer SRE.

Open questions for RetailCo (to resolve prior to POC kickoff):
- Can they provide a temporary outbound jump host for signed bundle verification during install? (yes/no)
- Which HSM vendor and OS kernel modules are available? (need exact model + firmware)
- Is local registry already in place and reachable from target VLANs? Provide registry FQDN/IP and auth method.
- Are there any blocklists that would prevent NTP/DNS to internal resolvers? We need consistent time.
- Who owns change approvals (name + contact) and what is the lead time for a CAB?

Risks and contingency plan:
- Risk: Bundle corrupted during transfer. Contingency: provide step-by-step verification and pair with checksum+signature verification and a fallback to retransfer via SFTP.
- Risk: HSM integration fails due to missing kernel module. Contingency: fallback to Vault running on dedicated host in customer network for POC with clearly documented limitations.
- Risk: Performance degradation on actual hardware. Contingency: reduce batch size and sequence length, test quantized model to reduce memory/compute.

Action items (owner, due):
- Maya: draft offline bundle builder + verification script, attach example bundle (2025-09-19).
- Jon: produce matrix of supported GPU drivers + recommended kernel versions (2025-09-17).
- Priya: KMS adapter example and Vault fallback doc (2025-09-20).
- RetailCo infra: provide filled inventory template and registry endpoint (2025-09-18).

Notes-to-self / workshop prep:
- Bring sample signed bundle and local registry load demo.
- Prepare short explainer slide for non-technical security reviewers showing data flows (no egress for model inference).
- Confirm we can run minimal console locally (no data plane egress) and prepare screenshots.

References & helpful links:
- internal runbook: CONF-3142 (deployment patterns)
- previous POC: PS-452 (a similar air-gapped retail deployment from 2024)
- build script PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments/pull/78

Bottom line: POC is feasible but requires offlined-bundle process + clear KMS/HSM plan. Primary gating items are: (1) registry/artifact ingestion process and (2) HSM/KMS compatibility. Once those two are agreed, the rest is standard ops and a 2–4 week timeline looks reasonable.
